declarations.parity_review: Reviewed loads a relative screenshot from the chat project. Original bodies, setup, imports, lifecycle and every actual/expected operand match the existing bounded source audit, including the enclosing function binding checks. Six completion structural controls pass. Buffer equality is limited to two ordinary built-in Buffers with exact byte indices and an unchanged built-in toJSON method; customized Buffers and non-Buffer operands are rejected. Vitest replay reconstructs the actual Buffer operands. Dynamic toBe comparisons preserve the original object/function identity using the fixture WeakMap reference IDs, with raw objects guarded against custom JSON, getters, symbol properties, cycles and reserved markers. Seventeen value-domain controls and seventy-two Buffer/identity Vitest/Rust verdicts pass, including equal bytes with distinct buffers and identical-looking objects with different identities. Every observation and an opposing counterexample agree between real Vitest and the Rust comparator. Detailed per-site bindings, inputs, observation counts, skipped-helper proofs and hashes: .jait/artifacts/parity-variants/source-checkpoint/.jait/artifacts/parity-values/combined-selected.json. The passing full translated report and internal/managed profiles are bound to the unchanged frozen source checkpoint. Live candidate sources, fixtures, Rust rules and transport hashes match that checkpoint. This is preservation of the reference tests for the exercised domains, not native-runtime or complete security assurance.
